title: Ohrid vs Kotor: Which Balkan Gem Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Ohrid and Kotor based on Reddit discussions, real costs, UNESCO heritage, crowds, and traveler experiences.

categories.title: 🌊 Atmosphere & Vibe
categories.summary: Ohrid is an ancient lakeside city with an authentic, unhurried vibe. Kotor is a dramatic Venetian walled city in a fjord-like bay — beautiful but busier in summer.
highlights: Ohrid wins on authenticity and price
Kotor wins on dramatic scenery and Adriatic access

categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Ohrid is significantly cheaper — roughly 50-60% less per day than Kotor. Budget accommodation starts at €10-18 vs €20-40 in Kotor. A lakeside dinner for two costs €15-25 vs €35-60.
highlights: Ohrid: €25-45/day mid-range
Kotor: €60-100/day mid-range

categories.title: ⛩️ Heritage & History
categories.summary: Both are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Ohrid is 2,000+ years old and where the Cyrillic alphabet was created. Kotor has Venetian fortifications from the 13th-18th centuries.
highlights: Ohrid: 365 churches, ancient theater, birthplace of Cyrillic
Kotor: 4.5km Venetian walls, medieval cathedral

categories.title: 🍽️ Food & Dining
categories.summary: Ohrid excels in value — freshwater trout, burek, and lakeside dining for €6-12/person. Kotor offers Adriatic seafood and Njeguši cured meats at higher prices.
highlights: Ohrid: budget-friendly, very good local food
Kotor: excellent seafood and prosciutto, higher prices

categories.title: 🏖️ Swimming & Beaches
categories.summary: Lake Ohrid offers crystal-clear freshwater swimming right in town. Kotor Bay is not ideal for swimming, but Budva (30 min away) has excellent Adriatic beaches.
highlights: Ohrid: lake swimming in town
Kotor: sea beaches via day trip to Budva

categories.title: 👥 Crowds & Tourism
categories.summary: Ohrid gets busy with Balkan vacationers in July-August but never at Kotor's cruise-ship scale. Kotor's old town floods with day-trippers from cruise ships each morning.
highlights: Ohrid: manageable crowds year-round
Kotor: cruise ships add thousands in peak summer

categories.title: 🚌 Getting Around
categories.summary: Both cities are walkable. Ohrid connects by bus to Skopje (2.5h), Tirana (4h). Kotor connects to Dubrovnik (2h), Budva (30 min), and Tivat Airport (20 min).
highlights: Kotor has better Adriatic circuit connectivity
Ohrid is well-linked to regional Balkans routes

categories.title: 🌤️ Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Shoulder season (May-June, Sep-Oct) is best for both. Summer is hot and crowded; Kotor is worse due to cruise ships. Ohrid is excellent even in winter.
highlights: Best for both: May-June, September-October
Avoid: July-August for crowds and heat

categories.title: 🗺️ Day Trips
categories.summary: Ohrid's lake boat tour (St. Naum, €15-30) is unmissable. Kotor's Perast and the Lovćen mountain drive are among the Balkans' best short excursions.
highlights: Ohrid: lake boat tours, Struga, Albania side of lake
Kotor: Perast, Budva, Cetinje, Lovćen National Park

categories.title: 🔀 Why Not Both?
categories.summary: Ohrid and Kotor are commonly combined in a 10-14 day Balkans loop: Dubrovnik → Kotor → Albania → Ohrid → Skopje. The journey between them takes 7-10 hours.
highlights: Standard Balkans circuit includes both
Route through Shkodër or Tirana to break the journey
